title: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. goes on concussion IL after collision at third base
content:
Following a collision at third base on Friday and subsequent concussion protocol testing, the Toronto Blue Jays have placed Vladimir Guerrero Jr. on the 7-day concussion IL. Guerrero must progress through MLB’s return-to-play protocols before rejoining Toronto, leaving an opening at first base for the Jays.

The incident, which happened in the sixth inning of Friday’s 3-1 win over the New York Yankees, saw Guerrero take an errant knee to the head during a series of defensive miscues by the Yankees. Guerrero, who was sliding into third base, collided with George Lombard Jr.’s knee. Guerrero was able to pop up to his feet and run home and score; however, field cameras caught the slugger wincing.

Guerrero was subsequently removed from the game and went through the concussion protocol, with Schneider noting postgame that Guerrero had “a bit of a headache.” He felt similar Saturday morning, the manager said.

“When you’re dealing with this,” Schneider said, “it’s really driven by the medical team.”

Just before first pitch on Saturday, Toronto made it official by placing Guerrero on the IL as part of a series of roster moves. Elsewhere, outfielder Daz Cameron had his contract selected, while right-hander Lazaro Estrada was designated for assignment.

Kazuma Okamoto and Charles McAdoo are expected to fill the bulk of time at first base for the Jays in Guerrero’s absence. Replacing his offensive production, though, may not be as difficult as it would’ve been in other years. Guerrero is in the midst of his worst professional season, hitting just seven homers in 115 games with a .693 OPS. He’s gone over a year without hitting a regular season home run at Rogers Centre. Still, the Jays’ lineup is often built around Guerrero and he will now be absent from the middle of the order for at least a week.

Cameron, a former top prospect with 160 MLB games, joined the Jays on a minor-league deal earlier this year after a stint in the KBO. The 29-year-old is expected to contribute in both corner-outfield spots for the Jays after hitting .367 with a 1.045 OPS in 23 Triple-A games.

“Could have went a couple of different ways,” Schneider said, “but I think you know you want to call a guy up when he’s doing well.”

Estrada, who was optioned to Triple A on Friday, has filled in admirably for the Jays at times this year but was out of options due to MLB’s new option maximum and getting sent to the minors five times this year. If Estrada clears waivers, he could rejoin the Jays before going to Triple-A Buffalo.
